To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a superconducting magnet has been built and tested, which is able to generate a 3 T magnetic field in 0.5 s, with a maximum pulsed loss of 0.6 J.
we have designed and built a superconducting magnet capable of producing a pulsed magnetic field of up to 3 Tesla at 4.2 K.
the magnet is capable of producing up to 2.9 T at a ramp rate of 6 T/s, with an efficiency of 0.7 W/kg at 4.5 T and a loss of 0.5 J/kg at 2.9.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a magnetic refrigerator for cooling of large-scale superconducting magnets.
a pulsed superconductive magnet, designed to be operated at a temperature below 4.5K.
the development and application of a novel magnetic refrigeration cycle, based on the magnetic properties of the superconductor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnet is performing very well.
the magnet is fully functional and meets the design goals.
this magnet, which is designed to operate at a temperature below 4.5 K, can be operated at a temperature of 1.8 K, with a maximum field of 2.9 T and a ramping rate up to 6.5 T/s.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pulsed superconductivity magnet is successfully developed and the performance of the magnet has been measured.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of a pulsed superconductive magnet for a 1.8-4.5 K magnetic refrigerator.
the magnet is a reliable, low-loss and low-cost device, which is well suited for a 1.8-4.5 K magnetic refrigeration cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a pulsed superconductor magnet can be built to produce high fields at high rates, with low losses and good field quality, at low cost, by using low-loss NbTi wire in a composite matrix, and commercially pure iron laminations.
the pulsed magnet can be operated at a high repetition frequency, with a duty cycle of up to 50% for a given field level.

the magnet design and construction techniques we have developed can be applied successfully to the construction of other pulsed superconductors, and that the magnet can be operated reliably at high ramping rate and low losses, which makes it suitable for the application envisaged.
